results.title: Data quality and rubrics: how to build trust in your models | Snorkel AI
results.content: # Data quality and rubrics: how to build trust in your models. *Your AI model is only as good as your data! While the AI industry races toward more sophisticated AI applications like agentic systems, a critical question remains top of mind: How do we *systematically* evaluate and improve the quality of training and evaluation data that powers these systems? It’s time for enterprises investing in AI to adopt the state-of-the-art approach used by major AI labs and Snorkel: structured evaluation rubrics. Welcome to Snorkel AI’s five-part blog series on rubrics. 1. Part 1 introduces rubric-based evaluation and how both automated and human evaluations benefit from using them. 4. Part 4 is another deep dive, this time into Snorkel’s own use of rubrics in a complex, multi-review process that integrates automated and human-in-the-loop evaluations that produce meaningful data outcomes and improvements to the rubrics over time. The shift to generative models and agentic systems requires a similar shift in how we approach evaluation.

results.title: Frontiers | LLM-as-a-Judge: automated evaluation of search query parsing using large language models
results.content: # LLM-as-a-Judge: automated evaluation of search query parsing using large language models. We propose a general framework for evaluating structured outputs using LLMs, focusing on search query parsing within an online classified platform. These results validate LLM-driven evaluation as a scalable, interpretable, and effective alternative to traditional evaluation methods, providing robust query parsing for real-world search systems. Figure 1 shows the parsing of an example search query in an online ads platform and a sketch of the evaluation process proposed in this work. Flowchart depicting the process of evaluating a search query for a “2+1 apartment for rent in Sefaköy.” Initially, the query undergoes “Search Query Parsing.” It categorizes under “Real Estate” with attributes like “room_count” and “explicit_keyword.” After classification, an “LLM as a Judge” assesses the query, resulting in an “evaluation” of “PASS” and providing an “explanation.”. By integrating LLM-as-a-Judge methods, we ensure a more robust and scalable evaluation of search query parsing in large-scale, real-world search systems, where accuracy and efficiency are critical.
